brief.subject: Diesel drops 16.5 cents as spot rates jump early
brief.headline: Diesel falls to $6.127 while holiday spot rates take off early
brief.dek: Fuel relief, an early spot-rate run, Mexico tariff threats and a court win for New York on non-domiciled CDLs.
brief.lede: Diesel fell 16.5 cents to $6.127 a gallon, giving carriers some margin relief just as spot rates climb earlier than usual ahead of the holidays.

sections.heading: Diesel eases again
bullets: $6.127 per gallon: U.S. average retail diesel for the week of 2026-11-09.
Down 16.5 cents (2.6%) week over week, a meaningful cut to per-mile fuel cost.
Down 5.2 cents over four weeks, so the trend is finally moving in carriers' favor.

sections.heading: Spot rates move early
bullets: Spot rates are rising ahead of the holidays, earlier than the usual seasonal pattern.
Small carriers with open capacity may find better-paying loads now rather than waiting for December.
Pressure remains: truck count is at its lowest since early 2022, with some carriers facing layoffs and bankruptcies.

sections.heading: Mexico trade: tariffs and traffic
bullets: Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless migrant caravans are halted, effective immediately if imposed.
$75.4B: U.S.-Mexico truck freight value in September, so any tariff jump could hit cross-border volume.
400 trucks: added Texas cross-border traffic from a Saturday crossing pilot.
Three bills in Congress would restrict presidential tariff power, though none is law yet.

sections.heading: Court sides with NY on CDLs
bullets: A unanimous Second Circuit panel ruled for New York in its fight with DOT over non-domiciled CDLs.
The case centered on federal funding denied over how long those CDLs can stay valid.
Watch for ripple effects on driver eligibility and state licensing rules.

sections.heading: Fraud and port delays
bullets: $150 million-plus in AI equipment stolen from June 2025 to June 2026, per Overhaul.
92% of incidents involved fake carrier identities or falsified documents, raising vetting scrutiny for legitimate small carriers.
Over nine days: rail dwell for containers at the Port of Los Angeles, which can disrupt drayage schedules.
